focus: Convergence and stop policy: whether convergence.cjs and reduce-state.cjs own stopPolicy, minIterations and the four convergence modes, vs convergence.md and the step_check_convergence algorithm
answeredQuestions: Convergence (v4.0.0.3, v4.0.0.16): do runtime/scripts/convergence.cjs and deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs honor stopPolicy, minIterations and the four convergence modes as deep-research/references/convergence/convergence.md documents?

graphEvents.label: Who owns stopPolicy and minIterations: code or YAML prose?
Neither convergence.cjs nor reduce-state.cjs reads stopPolicy or minIterations
Documented 3-signal rolling/MAD/entropy vote has no implementation; code uses a 5-signal graph composite

label: No code component owns the stop policy: convergence.cjs (944 lines) and reduce-state.cjs contain zero occurrences of stopPolicy, minIterations, maxIterations or max-iterations. Both concepts live only in deep-research-auto.yaml prose (stop_policy defined at :643, sole effect at :776). Any direct caller of convergence.cjs gets STOP_ALLOWED/STOP_BLOCKED with no minIterations floor and no stopPolicy awareness.

Two incompatible convergence math models. Documented (three-signal-model.md:25): rolling average of newInfoRatio (0.30) + MAD noise floor (0.35) + question entropy coverage (0.35), stop above 0.60. Implemented (convergence.cjs:329): questionCoverage 0.30 + claimVerificationRate 0.25 + inverted contradictionDensity 0.15 + sourceDiversity 0.15 + evidenceDepth 0.15. No shared signal, no shared weight, and 0.60 is not a constant anywhere in the entrypoint.

three-signal-model.md section 3 'Implementation' lists exactly three rows, all reference markdown (convergence.md, state-format.md, loop-protocol.md) and zero code. The feature catalog is self-refuting evidence that the feature has no implementation, yet still passes as a SOURCE FILES contract.

Every --config-json knob is unreachable from the workflow. convergence.cjs accepts configJson and reads antiConvergence.convergenceMode, config.slidingWindowSize and config.min_observations from it, but deep-research-auto.yaml:759 passes only --spec-folder --loop-type --session-id --convergence-mode --persist-snapshot --iteration. So antiConvergence.slidingWindowSize is silently ignored (window can only ever be the built-in 5, convergence.cjs:38) and readObservationThresholdConfig (convergence.cjs:274) is dead from the workflow path.

minIterations is enforced entirely by YAML prose and documented nowhere. The workflow extracts, defaults, warns on, clamps, enforces and logs it (auto.yaml:637,638,752,815,846), while convergence.md mentions minIterations exactly once, inside the divergent-pivot exclusion list at line 68. An operator reading the convergence reference cannot discover the field that can veto a stop.

divergent mode crosses a code/prose boundary no code bridges. convergence.cjs:42 accepts 'divergent' as a valid mode and computes convergence normally, but the pivot is triggered only by auto.yaml:862 branching on a prose-computed reason string, with a seven-value exclusion list (convergence.md:68) that only prose can enforce. A runtime-accepted mode changes nothing in the runtime.

Improvement: move the stop-policy and minIterations decision into convergence.cjs by passing --config-json from the workflow and emitting the reason strings (minIterationsNotReached, stopPolicySuppressed) from code. Collapses f-iter003-001/004/005/006 into one owned contract and lets convergence.md document what the tool returns rather than what the workflow hopes.

This lineage runs stopPolicy 'max-iterations', so per auto.yaml:776 the inline vote can never set STOP or BLOCKED and only max_iterations terminates. Observed ratio 0.72 -> 0.68 with 2/11 questions answered and stuck count 0 is exactly what that policy prescribes; the behaviour matches the contract and cannot be attributed to the drift.

direction: convergence.cjs silently drops the sliding-window size argument
reason: It does not drop an argument; the workflow never supplies one and never supplies --config-json, so the override path is unreachable rather than ignored. Recorded as f-iter003-004 with the correct mechanism.

direction: stop_policy is a dead template variable in deep-research-auto.yaml
reason: It is consumed at auto.yaml:776, which makes the inline 3-signal vote telemetry-only under max-iterations. The defect is ownership (no code reads it), not deadness.
